'''''Hyacinthoides paivae''''' is a species of bluebell in the genus ''[[Hyacinthoides]]'' native to the north-western part of the [[Iberian Peninsula]]. It lives chiefly in shady woodlands, and grows up to {{convert|45|cm|abbr=on}} tall, producing a cluster of up to 18 pale blue flowers in spring. It was formally described in 1996, having previously been identified as belonging to the related species ''[[Hyacinthoides italica|H. italica]]''.

==Description==
''Hyacinthoides paivae'' is a [[perennial plant]] which grows from [[bulb]]s that are typically {{convert|17|-|30|mm}} × {{convert|13|-|30|mm|abbr=on}}.<ref name="Ortiz"/><ref name="FI">{{cite book |author=S. Ortiz |year=2011 |chapter=''Hyacinthoides'' Heist. ex Fabr. |title=Flora Iberica |volume=20 |chapter-url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/imprenta/tomoXX/20_183_00_Hyacinthoides.pdf |title-link=Flora Iberica }}</ref> Each bulb produces 4–7 (more rarely 2–12) basal leaves, each {{convert|20|-|50|cm}} long and {{convert|7|-|12|mm|abbr=on}} wide.<ref name="Ortiz"/><ref name="FI"/> The stems are {{convert|22|-|45|cm|abbr=on}} long, and bear an [[inflorescence]] comprising 6–18 flowers in a multilateral [[raceme]].<ref name="Ortiz"/><ref name="FI"/> Each flower is attached by a [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] {{convert|5|-|7|mm|abbr=on}} long, and is itself {{convert|12|-|22|mm|abbr=on}} long by {{convert|2|-|3|mm|2|abbr=on}} wide.<ref name="Ortiz"/><ref name="FI"/> ''H. paivae'' can be told apart from ''H. italica'' by its broader leaves and larger flowers; ''H. hispanica'' differs in having longer, narrower, unscented and bell-shaped flowers.<ref name="Ortiz"/>

==Distribution and ecology==
''Hyacinthoides paivae'' is [[endemism|endemic]] to the north-western part of the [[Iberian Peninsula]], including western parts of [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]] ([[Province of A Coruña|A Coruña]], [[Province of Ourense|Ourense]] and [[Province of Pontevedra|Pontevedra]] provinces) and north-western parts of [[Portugal]] ([[Beira Litoral Province|Beira Litoral]], [[Douro Litoral Province|Douro Litoral]], [[Minho Province|Minho]] and [[Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro Province|Trás-os-Montes]] provinces).<ref name="FI"/> Material of an unidentified species from the [[Sierra de la Demanda]], a small mountain range on the border between [[Province of Burgos|Burgos province]] and [[La Rioja (Spain)|La Rioja]], matches ''H. paivae'' genetically.<ref name="Grundmann"/>

[[File:Berne botanic garden Hyacinthoides italica.jpg|thumb|upright|''H.paivae'' was confused with this species, ''[[Hyacinthoides italica|H. italica]]'', seen growing at the [[Berne Botanical Gardens]].]]
''H. paivae'' occurs in oak woodland and pine woods growing over ''[[Ulex]]'', ''[[Erica cinerea]]'' and ''[[Cistus]]'' spp., as well as other shady habitats. It also occurs occasionally on coastal cliffs, and in mown meadows.<ref name="Ortiz"/> The typical [[flowering period]] is March and April, although it can be as late as June in upland areas, such as [[Monte Pindo]].<ref name="Ortiz"/>

==Taxonomic history==
In 1990, bluebells assigned to the species ''[[Hyacinthoides italica]]'' were reported from north-western Spain. Later analyses of the species [[morphology (biology)|morphology]] demonstrated that the plants did not belong to ''H. italica'', which is only otherwise found near the [[France|French]]–[[Italy|Italian]] border.<ref name="Ortiz">{{cite journal |author1=Santiago Ortiz |author2=Juan Rodríguez-Oubiña |year=1996 |title=Taxonomic characterization of populations of ''Hyacinthoides'' sect. ''Somera'' (Hyacinthaceae) in the northwestern Iberian Peninsula |journal=[[Plant Systematics and Evolution]] |volume=202 |issue=1–2 |pages=111–119 |doi=10.1007/BF00985820|bibcode=1996PSyEv.202..111O |s2cid=32184114 }}</ref> Instead, it was realised that they represented a new species, which was named ''Hyacinthoides paivae'' by Santiago Ortiz and Juan Rodríguez-Oubiña in 1996, the [[specific name (botany)|specific epithet]] ''{{lang|la|paivae}}'' honouring the Portuguese botanist Jorge Paiva.<ref name="Ortiz"/>

The [[holotype]], a specimen from [[Dumbría]], [[Province of A Coruña|A Coruña province]], Spain, is held at the [[herbarium]] of the ''{{lang|es|[[University of Santiago de Compostela|Universidad de Santiago de Compostela]]}}''; [[Isotype (biology)|isotypes]] are also kept there, and at the [[University of Coimbra]], the ''{{lang|es|[[Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid|Real Jardín Botánico]]}}'' and ''{{lang|es|[[Complutense University of Madrid|Universidad Complutense]]}}'' in Madrid, the ''{{lang|es|Centro de Investigaciones Forestales y Ambientales de Lourizán}}'' in [[Pontevedra]], and at the [[Natural History Museum, London|Natural History Museum]] and [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] in London.<ref name="FI"/>

Ortiz and Rodríguez-Oubiña initially placed the species in "''Hyacinthoides'' sect. ''Somera''", but more recent [[molecular phylogenetics|molecular phylogenetic]] analysis could not confirm any of the existing [[section (botany)|sections]] in the genus, and placed it instead in an informal group alongside ''[[Hyacinthoides non-scripta|H. non-scripta]]'', ''[[Hyacinthoides hispanica|H. hispanica]]'' and ''[[Hyacinthoides cedretorum|H. cedretorum]]''.<ref name="Grundmann">{{cite journal |author1=Michael Grundmann |author2=Fred J. Rumsey |author3=Stephen W. Ansell |author4=Stephen J. Russell |author5=Sarah C. Darwin |author6=Johannes C. Vogel |author7=Mark Spencer |author8=Jane Squirrell |author9=Peter M. Hollingsworth |author10=Santiago Ortiz |author11=Harald Schneider |year=2010 |title=Phylogeny and taxonomy of the bluebell genus ''Hyacinthoides'', Asparagaceae [Hyacinthaceae] |journal=[[Taxon (journal)|Taxon]] |volume=59 |issue=1 |pages=68–82 |doi=10.1002/tax.591008 }}</ref>
